title: Model Terrain Audit: competitive economics probe and fieldwork
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Run a focused ‘Model Terrain Audit’ combining automated telemetry probes, synthetic workload microbenchmarks, and 6–8 buyer interviews to produce a prioritized map of competitor model economics, substitution risk, and enterprise integration friction. Deliver a repeatable kit (templates, telemetry dashboard, and interview script) to operationalize continuous market monitoring.
goals: Quantify per-request and per-token economic differences across top 5 external model providers for representative Redwood workloads
Surface 10 signal types that predict model substitution risk (latency spikes, token-price deltas, API behavior drift, quantization artifacts, regional availability events)
Create a ready-to-run telemetry probe and dashboard to run weekly comparatives and surface alerts to PM + SRE
Capture buyer stories and procurement constraints from 6 enterprise customers to validate substitution sensitivity and SLAs
deliverables: Telemetry probe code and runbook (bench harness + scripts) in GH: synthetic prompt sets, payload generator, cost calc
Model Terrain Audit deck: 20-slide executive summary with economics tables, risk heatmap, recommended fallbacks
Dashboard: weekly comparative showing latency, p50/p95, token cost per output, error rate, and availability by region
Interview synthesis doc and canonical interview script for sales/solutions to capture procurement constraints
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry probe reproduces results for at least 3 representative workloads (short chat, long-context RAG, embeddings) and is documented in GH
Dashboard surfaces top-3 substitution signals and can produce an automated alert when a supplier moves beyond threshold
Interview synthesis includes verbatim buyer constraints and 3 validated procurement thresholds (latency, cost, data residency)
PM review approves the Audit deck and OSS runbook for internal reuse
stakeholders: Product: Marcus Leung (assignee), Priya Rao (lead PM analytics)
Legal: compliance review for interview recordings
steps: 1) Define 3 synthetic workloads and canonical prompt sets (short chat, RAG long context, embeddings) - target: 2026-03-14
2) Implement telemetry probe harness and cost model (GH PR draft) - target: 2026-03-18
3) Run cross-provider microbench (hosted, dedicated sim, private sim) across us-east and eu-west - target: 2026-03-21
4) Stitch results into dashboard and compute substitution indices - target: 2026-03-24
5) Conduct 6 buyer interviews using canonical script; synthesize procurement thresholds - target: 2026-03-28
6) Assemble Audit deck and Ops runbook; PM and SRE review - target: 2026-03-31
7) Publish dashboard, add alert rules, handoff to Signals team - target: 2026-04-02
risks: Telemetry limitations: provider rate-limits or inconsistent metrics could invalidate comparisons
Sampling bias: synthetic workloads might not reflect customer workloads — mitigated by selecting three representative workloads and validating with customers
Interview availability: difficulty booking enterprise procurement interviews within the sprint window
Legal/Privacy: buyer interview recordings require approvals causing schedule slips
